title: How can I run a PHP script inside a HTML file?

content:
# The Execution Model Behind HTML and PHP Files The core misunderstanding in asking how to run PHP code inside an `.html` file usually stems from a confusion about server-side execution versus client-side rendering. You cannot execute PHP logic directly within a standard `.html` file because the web browser does not possess a PHP runtime environment. When a request arrives at your server, the web server acts as a gatekeeper. If the file extension is `.html`, the server treats the content as static text and sends it to the browser without invoking any server-side interpreters. The code remains hidden inside the source, effectively dead code that the browser will never interpret. To execute PHP logic, the request must reach a script with a specific extension that signals the web server to pass the file to the PHP interpreter first. This typically means renaming the file from `.html` to `.php`. Once renamed, the server processes the file, executes the PHP tags, and sends only the resulting HTML back to the client. This separation ensures security by preventing users from executing arbitrary code on your server simply by viewing a page. ### Implementing Mixed Content in a Single Request If your goal is to display standard HTML while injecting dynamic data or logic, you do not need to merge the languages into a single file type. Instead, you use a PHP wrapper file that loads the static content. Consider a scenario where you want a landing page with a header and footer generated by PHP, but a specific section containing complex JavaScript or static assets. You would create a file named `index.php` and include your HTML structure within it.
